newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram says tax revenues seen rising.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram says tax revenues seen rising.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday the ratio of direct taxes as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) had risen to 3.0 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) from 2.0 percent in 1990/91.
"The strategy of reducing taxes and better enforcement is yielding results," he told a news conference.
In the 1997/98 budget Chidambaram slashed the tax rate for the highest personal income bracket to 30 percent from 40, and the corporate tax rate to 35 percent from 40.

In the current fiscal year beginning April 1 India hoped to raise tax revenues from income and corporate taxes by 15 percent, from excise duties by 13 percent and from customs duties by 19 percent compared to 1996/97, Chidambaram said.
He did not give actual figures .
"The goal is to raise about 450 billion rupees ($12.6 billion) as direct taxes and to raise 1,050 billion rupees as indirect taxes," Chidamabaram said.
The government on Wednesday launched a new tax amnesty scheme called the Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme (VDIS) to widen the scope of taxes in the country.
"It is a scheme to motivate people to voluntarily disclose undisclosed income which may or may not have been translated into wealth," Chidambaram said.
The VDIS, which had been broadly outlined in the 1997/98 budget presented on February 28, would begin on July 1 and end on December 31.
The six-month scheme aimed to draw tax evaders who operated in the shadows of the "parallel economy" into the tax net.
Private economists say at least four of every 10 rupees earned in India are generated in the black economy and never declared to authorities.
Asked about the amount of money to be raised under the VDIS, Chidambaram said: "I have a well-crafted strategy and do not want to disclose it right now."
Chidambaram hoped that tax compliance within the economy would improve.
He pledged to strengthen the administrative machinery and infrastructure of the tax departments to achieve a higher rate of collection. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
